implementation.peer_publication: Authenticated publish/query RPCs bind caller, reporter, placement group, proposal, chosen input and canonical plan. Both wire routes require a trusted materializer.
implementation.custody: First publication syncs retained quorum input before kernel publication. Learner promotion keeps exclusive cell ownership through synchronous transfer into the voter map.
implementation.historical_retry: Replay-proven active ancestry permits historical acknowledgements after newer views and promises. Retry applies the current committed prefix and preserves original PUBLICATION bytes, generations, log, receipts, promises and primary-contact clocks.
implementation.cold_decision: The same retained decision journal recovers through its chosen input, sealed stage and active ancestry even when its initial authority differs. This cannot create a new acceptor or reset promises.
implementation.application_failure: Failed current-prefix application leaves installation pending. Warm stage receipt reuse requires matching recovery state and no pending application; failed attempts clear stale receipt tokens.
implementation.transport: One bounded retry resolves transient publication/query transport failures. Semantic errors and authenticated reporter mismatches are rejected.

tls_regressions: Permanent deletion of original source and nominated candidate; surviving voter and learner publish, cold-open promoted role, elect another candidate and commit later operations.
Exact 128 KiB operation, original request receipt and accepted tail survive publication, later views, promises and repeated cold recovery.
Warm and cold historical retries preserve original proof bytes, active pointer, generations and exact manifest/segment bytes; later application work is rebuilt.
Wrong caller/input/plan/group, missing materializer, failed application and corrupt promoted owner cannot acknowledge readiness.
Application failure after durable authority publication resumes cold without another generation or log rewrite.
Real TLS reply suppression resolves exactly once through the production dispatcher; an authenticated connection cannot return a report naming another voter.

fixture_failure.cause: The readback fixture attempted a second SegmentStore open while a child peer owned the store lock.
fixture_failure.fix: Read exact manifest and segment bytes without taking ownership or running recovery. Passing focused and affected-package runs include this fix.

limits: Native daemon transition configuration and bounded background orchestration are not wired by this change.
A collected publication quorum is historical evidence; durable global completion and replicated control/catalog admission remain unfinished. No operator membership command is enabled.
Repeated transitions, removed-role lifecycle, abort/conflict handling, independent-group routing, retention and legacy migration remain required.
The TLS fixtures use trusted protocol-entry application and do not establish SQL/KV/object/blob semantics across a live native membership transition.
Local host tests do not qualify independent hosts/regions, power loss, production capacity/p99 targets, or deterministic native socket/thread scheduling.
The passing scoped Clippy command excludes existing dependency lint debt.
